page: Vultr vx1-m-16c-128g-960s is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 128.0 GB of system memory, which provides a high density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier (top 10%). Text processing via Geekbench and text generation for small 135M parameter language models also achieve top-tier performance. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core scores, falls within the average range. Memory performance is strong, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25%, while uncached memory bandwidth and database operations remain average.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated AMD EPYC processor allocation, this server type offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads without the premium of GPU-accelerated hardware. The combination of 128.0 GB RAM and a 960 GB NVMe SSD makes it highly suitable for hosting relational databases, in-memory caching layers, text processing pipelines, and small-scale language model inference.
